title: Unpinned third-party action
why: A tag or branch ref is a pointer the action's maintainer — or anyone who can retag it — can move to different code after you have reviewed it. Only a full-length commit SHA names one immutable revision.
fix: Pin the ref to a full 40-character commit SHA and keep the tag in a trailing comment, e.g. actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
message: Action is pinned by tag or branch, not a commit SHA — FLAG for review: the tag can be moved to new code under you.

title: Pull-request-target with a head checkout
why: pull_request_target runs in the base repository's context: it receives a read/write GITHUB_TOKEN and can read repository secrets. Checking out the pull request's own head puts attacker-authored files on disk in that context.
fix: Use pull_request instead of pull_request_target, or drop the head checkout and work only from the base branch, or split the job so nothing from the fork runs in the privileged workflow.
message: This runs untrusted pull-request code with a write-scoped token and secrets in scope — FLAG for review: confirm why pull_request_target is needed and whether the head checkout can go.

title: Interpolation into run
why: GitHub substitutes the expression into the script text before the shell ever sees it, so a title, body or branch name containing quotes or command substitution becomes shell syntax.
fix: Pass the value through env: and reference the variable, quoting it in the shell: env: {TITLE: "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"} then run: echo "$TITLE"
message: Untrusted event data is interpolated directly into a shell step — FLAG for review: pass it through `env:` and quote the variable.

title: Over-scoped workflow token
why: permissions: write-all, or a job that pushes or publishes without declaring permissions at all, hands whatever runs in that job the ability to write to the repository.
fix: Declare the scopes the job needs and nothing else — usually permissions: {contents: read} at workflow level, and contents: write only on the one job that has to write.
message: The workflow token carries more scope than this job needs — FLAG for review: grant only the scopes this job needs.

title: Self-hosted runner on an untrusted trigger
why: A self-hosted runner keeps state between jobs. A pull request from a fork that lands on it can read what the previous job left behind and, on a long-lived host, reach whatever that host can reach.
fix: Use a GitHub-hosted runner for untrusted triggers, or run the self-hosted runner in an ephemeral, isolated, credential-free context with no network path to anything you care about.
message: A self-hosted runner receives work from an untrusted trigger — FLAG for review: a fork can run code on that host; confirm it is ephemeral and isolated.

title: Secrets reachable by untrusted or logged code
why: A secret in env: or with: is in scope for every command that step runs, and a secret interpolated into a run: block can be printed into a log that outlives the job. persist-credentials leaves the token in .git/config for later steps to reuse.
fix: Keep secrets out of jobs that touch pull-request code, pass them by name through env: at the step that needs them, never echo them, and set persist-credentials: false when the checkout does not need to push.
message: This path can expose a secret to untrusted or logged code — FLAG for review: check whether the secret has to be in scope here at all.

title: Outsider-drivable trigger executing code
why: issue_comment, discussion_comment and workflow_run can be started by someone outside the repository. A job that then checks out and builds the repository, or installs an artefact the upstream run produced, runs content that outsider influenced.
fix: Gate the job on the upstream conclusion and on an allow-list of authors or labels, treat downloaded artefacts as untrusted input, and never pipe a download straight into a shell.
message: This trigger can be driven from outside the repository and the job executes code — FLAG for review: confirm the trust assumptions and add an upstream conclusion check.
